Choose one of the outlines gr_outline() compared

Source: R/outline-alternatives.R
gr_outline_pick.Rd

gr_outline() with alternatives above 1 returns its first proposal and attaches the others it kept. This hands back the one you choose, with its own claim assignment, rationale and closing section, so the headings, the claims placed under each and the claims they were derived from stay one consistent object. Copying attr(, "claims") from one outline onto another's headings is what this avoids: gr_synthesise() refuses a claim placed under a heading the outline does not have.

Usage

gr_outline_pick(outline, alternative)

Arguments

outline

A gr_outline() result made with alternatives above 1.

alternative

Which outline, by its number in attr(outline, "comparison")$alternative: 1 is the first proposal.

Value

The outline chosen, shaped like any gr_outline() result, without the alternatives and comparison attached.

Details

Nothing here ranks the outlines. attr(outline, "comparison") lays them side by side: how many sections each has, how many claims and how many contested claims each section holds, and how far each lies from the first proposal. Which grouping makes the review's argument is the author's call.

The outline returned carries attr(, "alternative"), which says which one it is. gr_synthesise() records it in $outline_alternative and in its trace, and gr_audit_report() says which was used, so a review written from the second proposal says so. Renaming its headings keeps that record. Moving claims between its sections does not: the grouping is then your own, and the review is recorded as one written from an outline of your own would be.

See also

gr_outline(), gr_synthesise()

Examples

tab <- data.frame(document = c("a.pdf", "b.pdf"), status = "ok",
                  duplicate_of = NA_character_, n_filled = 1L, n_unverified = 0L,
                  conflicts = NA_character_, design = c("trial", "survey"),
                  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
cl <- gr_mock_client(function(messages, params) {
  seen <- paste(unlist(lapply(messages, `[[`, "content")), collapse = " ")
  if (grepl("<earlier_outlines>", seen, fixed = TRUE)) {
    return(paste0('{"sections":[{"heading":"Trials find it","brief":"the trials",',
                  '"claims":[1],"rationale":"design"},{"heading":"Surveys do not",',
                  '"brief":"the surveys","claims":[2],"rationale":"design"}]}'))
  }
  if (grepl("<claims>", seen, fixed = TRUE)) {
    return(paste0('{"sections":[{"heading":"What it finds","brief":"the claims",',
                  '"claims":[1,2],"rationale":"one topic"}]}'))
  }
  paste0('{"claims":[{"claim":"It works in trials.","kind":"finding",',
         '"supported_by":[1],"contradicted_by":[],"moderator":null,"scope":null},',
         '{"claim":"Surveys find no effect.","kind":"finding",',
         '"supported_by":[2],"contradicted_by":[],"moderator":null,"scope":null}]}')
})
cm <- gr_claims(tab, question = "Does it work?", client = cl)
o <- gr_outline(cm, client = cl, alternatives = 2)
attr(o, "comparison")[, c("alternative", "sections", "claims_per_section", "distance")]
#>   alternative sections claims_per_section distance
#> 1           1        2               2, 0        0
#> 2           2        3            1, 1, 0        1
o2 <- gr_outline_pick(o, 2)
names(o2)
#> [1] "Trials find it"  "Surveys do not"  "What is missing"
attr(o2, "claims")
#>          section claim_id
#> 1 Trials find it        1
#> 2 Surveys do not        2
